subproblem.title: The explicit tangential-Jacobian matrix has the Gram determinant of Λ on an orthonormal basis of P (parent step 0)
subproblem.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) = ℝ^N with its standard orthonormal basis e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N), P ⊆ E a linear subspace with orthogonal projection p := P.starProjection, b = (b_a)_{a ∈ Fin k} an orthonormal basis of P, and Λ: E → E a continuous linear map. Then det[⟨Λpe_i, Λpe_j⟩ + ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩]_{i,j ∈ Fin N} = det[⟨Λb_a, Λb_c⟩]_{a,c ∈ Fin k}. In words: the explicit N×N matrix whose square-rooted determinant is the tangential Jacobian jac(Λ, P) used throughout this branch has the same determinant as the k×k Gram matrix of Λ on any orthonormal basis of P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))) (b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin k) ℝ P) (Λ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin N ↦ inner ℝ (Λ (P.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)))) (Λ (P.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))) + inner ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) - P.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) - P.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a c : Fin k ↦ inner ℝ (Λ (b a)) (Λ (b c)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof (the tangential Jacobian identity det S_P(Λ) = J^P(Λ)², which the parent obtains from the block-diagonal form of S_P(Λ) in an orthonormal basis adapted to P ⊕ P^⊥). Here the same block computation is carried out without completing b to a basis of E. No errata apply.

Notation. ⟨·,·⟩ is the inner product of E and δ is the Kronecker delta. For matrices, Xᵀ is the transpose and 1_m the m×m identity. S denotes the N×N matrix on the left-hand side, S_{ij} = ⟨Λpe_i, Λpe_j⟩ + ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩, and G the k×k matrix on the right-hand side, G_{ac} = ⟨Λb_a, Λb_c⟩ (b_a is regarded as a vector of E through the inclusion P ⊆ E). Let Bm be the real N×k matrix with Bm_{ia} := ⟨e_i, b_a⟩, the i-th coordinate of b_a.

1. Projection formula. For every x ∈ E, p x = Σ_a ⟨b_a, x⟩ b_a: this is the expansion of the orthogonal projection onto P in the orthonormal basis b of P (Mathlib: OrthonormalBasis.starProjection_eq_sum_rankOne, i.e. P.starProjection = Σ_a rankOne(b_a, b_a)). The real inner product is symmetric, so ⟨b_a, e_i⟩ = Bm_{ia}, and therefore p e_i = Σ_a Bm_{ia} b_a for every i.

2. Orthonormality. ⟨b_a, b_c⟩ = δ_{ac} for all a, c. Indeed b is orthonormal in P (OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal with orthonormal_iff_ite), and the inclusion P ⊆ E preserves inner products.

3. BmᵀBm = 1_k. For all a, c, (BmᵀBm)_{ac} = Σ_i ⟨e_i, b_a⟩⟨e_i, b_c⟩ = ⟨b_a, b_c⟩ = δ_{ac}. The middle equality is Parseval's identity for the orthonormal basis (e_i) of E (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner for EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose vectors are EuclideanSpace.single i 1). The last equality is step 2.

4. First summand. By step 1 and the linearity of Λ, Λpe_i = Σ_a Bm_{ia} Λb_a. By bilinearity of the inner product, ⟨Λpe_i, Λpe_j⟩ = Σ_a Σ_c Bm_{ia} Bm_{jc} ⟨Λb_a, Λb_c⟩ = Σ_a Σ_c Bm_{ia} G_{ac} Bm_{jc} = (Bm G Bmᵀ)_{ij}.

5. Second summand. Expanding, ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩ = ⟨e_i, e_j⟩ − ⟨e_i, pe_j⟩ − ⟨pe_i, e_j⟩ + ⟨pe_i, pe_j⟩. Each term is computed separately:
- ⟨e_i, e_j⟩ = δ_{ij}.
- By step 1, ⟨e_i, pe_j⟩ = Σ_a Bm_{ja}⟨e_i, b_a⟩ = Σ_a Bm_{ia}Bm_{ja}.
- By step 1, ⟨pe_i, e_j⟩ = Σ_a Bm_{ia}⟨b_a, e_j⟩ = Σ_a Bm_{ia}Bm_{ja}.
- By steps 1 and 2, ⟨pe_i, pe_j⟩ = Σ_a Σ_c Bm_{ia}Bm_{jc}δ_{ac} = Σ_a Bm_{ia}Bm_{ja}.
Hence ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩ = δ_{ij} − (Bm Bmᵀ)_{ij}.

6. Matrix form. By steps 4 and 5, S = Bm G Bmᵀ + 1_N − Bm Bmᵀ = 1_N + Bm Y, where Y is the k×N matrix Y := G Bmᵀ − Bmᵀ.

7. Determinant. The Weinstein–Aronszajn (Sylvester) identity states det(1_N + XW) = det(1_k + WX) for every N×k matrix X and every k×N matrix W (Mathlib: Matrix.det_one_add_mul_comm). Apply it with X = Bm and W = Y, then use step 3 (BmᵀBm = 1_k):
det S = det(1_N + Bm Y) = det(1_k + Y Bm) = det(1_k + G(BmᵀBm) − BmᵀBm) = det(1_k + G − 1_k) = det G.
This is the claim.

8. Degenerate cases. The argument is uniform in k and N.
- If k = 0 (P = 0): Bm is an N×0 matrix, so S = 1_N. Both determinants equal 1, because the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.
- If N = 0: then k = 0 as well, and both sides are empty determinants.

Imports: none beyond the frozen scope; all lemmas cited above are reachable from `import GMT.Ch04.Submission`.

Remark (relation to the parent's argument). Complete b by an orthonormal basis b' of P^⊥, and let O = [Bm | Bm'] be the resulting orthogonal matrix. Then O diag(G, 1) Oᵀ = Bm G Bmᵀ + Bm'Bm'ᵀ = Bm G Bmᵀ + 1_N − Bm Bmᵀ. By step 6 this equals S, which is the parent's block-diagonal statement det S = (det O)² det diag(G, 1) = det G. Steps 6–7 reach the same conclusion without choosing b'. ∎
proof_key_steps: Expand p e_i = Σ_a ⟨b_a, e_i⟩ b_a in the orthonormal basis b of P (starProjection_eq_sum_rankOne) and set Bm_{ia} := ⟨e_i, b_a⟩
BmᵀBm = 1_k by Parseval in the standard basis of E and orthonormality of b
Entrywise: ⟨Λpe_i, Λpe_j⟩ = (Bm G Bmᵀ)_{ij} and ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩ = δ_{ij} − (Bm Bmᵀ)_{ij}, so S = 1_N + Bm(G Bmᵀ − Bmᵀ)
Weinstein–Aronszajn det(1_N + XW) = det(1_k + WX) (Matrix.det_one_add_mul_comm) with BmᵀBm = 1_k gives det S = det(1_k + G − 1_k) = det G

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type match, including the orthonormal-basis hypothesis. Projection expansion and Parseval give BᵀB = I and S = I + B(GBᵀ − Bᵀ); Sylvester's determinant identity then proves exactly the claimed equality. The proof handles singular and zero-dimensional cases without extra assumptions and has no circular dependence.

subproblem.title: Countable gluing of an image-integral identity over a disjoint measurable partition (parent steps 2 and 5)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a type with a σ-algebra and μ a measure on X. Let f: X → X be injective, mapping μ-null sets to μ-null sets and μ-null-measurable sets to μ-null-measurable sets. Let Z ⊆ X be μ-null-measurable, (D_i)_{i∈ℕ} pairwise disjoint measurable sets with μ(Z ∖ ⋃_i D_i) = 0, and u, g: X → [0, ∞] arbitrary functions such that ∫⁻_{f(Z ∩ D_i)} u dμ = ∫⁻_{Z ∩ D_i} g dμ for every i. Then ∫⁻_{f(Z)} u dμ = ∫⁻_Z g dμ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (f : X → X) (Z : Set X) (D : ℕ → Set X) (u g : X → ℝ≥0∞), Function.Injective f → (∀ Y : Set X, μ Y = 0 → μ (f '' Y) = 0) → (∀ Y : Set X, NullMeasurableSet Y μ → NullMeasurableSet (f '' Y) μ) → NullMeasurableSet Z μ → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (D i)) → Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (D i) (D j)) → μ (Z \ ⋃ i, D i) = 0 → (∀ i, ∫⁻ y in f '' (Z ∩ D i), u y ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in Z ∩ D i, g x ∂μ) → ∫⁻ y in f '' Z, u y ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in Z, g x ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the summation argument of steps 2 and 5 of the parent proof (disjoint decomposition of M ∩ K into the pieces M_i = M ∩ K ∩ D_i up to the null set M ∩ K ∩ N₀, and of f(M ∩ K) into the f(M_i) up to a null set, followed by lintegral_iUnion₀ on both sides), stated for an abstract measure space. No errata apply.

1. The source side. Let R := Z ∖ ⋃_i D_i; by hypothesis μ(R) = 0. Then Z = R ∪ ⋃_i (Z ∩ D_i): a point of Z either lies in no D_i, in which case it lies in R, or it lies in some D_i, in which case it lies in Z ∩ D_i. Hence Z ∖ ⋃_i (Z ∩ D_i) ⊆ R is μ-null, while ⋃_i (Z ∩ D_i) ∖ Z = ∅. Therefore Z =ᵐ[μ] ⋃_i (Z ∩ D_i) (ae_eq_set).

2. The image side. Images commute with unions, so step 1 gives f(Z) = f(R) ∪ ⋃_i f(Z ∩ D_i), and μ(f(R)) = 0 because f maps null sets to null sets. Hence f(Z) ∖ ⋃_i f(Z ∩ D_i) ⊆ f(R) is μ-null. Also ⋃_i f(Z ∩ D_i) = f(⋃_i (Z ∩ D_i)) ⊆ f(Z), so the reverse difference is empty. Therefore f(Z) =ᵐ[μ] ⋃_i f(Z ∩ D_i).

3. Disjointness and measurability.
- Each Z ∩ D_i is μ-null-measurable, as the intersection of the null-measurable Z with the measurable D_i.
- The sets Z ∩ D_i (i ∈ ℕ) are pairwise disjoint, because the D_i are.
- f is injective, so the images f(Z ∩ D_i) are pairwise disjoint as well (Disjoint.image with f injective on X).
- Each f(Z ∩ D_i) is μ-null-measurable by the hypothesis on f.
Disjoint sets are in particular μ-a.e. disjoint.

4. Summation. Set-lintegrals over μ-a.e. equal sets coincide (setLIntegral_congr). The lintegral over a countable union of pairwise a.e.-disjoint null-measurable sets is the sum of the lintegrals (lintegral_iUnion₀). Neither fact needs measurability of the integrand. Hence
∫⁻_{f(Z)} u dμ
 = ∫⁻_{⋃_i f(Z∩D_i)} u dμ (step 2)
 = Σ_i ∫⁻_{f(Z∩D_i)} u dμ (step 3, lintegral_iUnion₀)
 = Σ_i ∫⁻_{Z∩D_i} g dμ (hypothesis, termwise)
 = ∫⁻_{⋃_i (Z∩D_i)} g dμ (step 3, lintegral_iUnion₀)
 = ∫⁻_Z g dμ (step 1).

5. Degenerate cases. No step uses Z ≠ ∅, finiteness of μ or measurability of u or g, so the argument covers these cases verbatim. For example, if Z = ∅ both sides are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Z = (Z ∖ ⋃ D_i) ∪ ⋃ (Z ∩ D_i) with μ-null remainder, so Z =ᵐ ⋃ (Z ∩ D_i)
f(Z) = f(remainder) ∪ ⋃ f(Z ∩ D_i) with f(remainder) null, so f(Z) =ᵐ ⋃ f(Z ∩ D_i)
Z ∩ D_i and f(Z ∩ D_i) are pairwise disjoint (f injective) and null-measurable (hypotheses)
setLIntegral_congr and lintegral_iUnion₀ on both sides, then sum the piecewise identities

audit.reason: The abstract measure-space prose matches the exact Lean proposition. Null preservation gives the image remainder equality almost everywhere; injectivity and null-measurability preservation justify disjoint measurable summation on the image side. Applying setLIntegral_congr and lintegral_iUnion₀ on both sides proves the conclusion for arbitrary weights. The proof is complete and independent of the other children and parent.

subproblem.title: Area formula for the image of a Borel subset of one injective Lipschitz piece under an injective Lipschitz map (parent steps 3(b)–(e))
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with standard orthonormal basis e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin (n+ℓ)), ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Hⁿ := μHE[n] on E. Let C ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel, F: ℝⁿ → E Lipschitz, differentiable at every point of C and injective on C; f: E → E Lipschitz; A ⊆ E Borel with A ⊆ F(C), f injective on A and differentiable at every point of A; P: E → {linear subspaces of E} any map with P(F(v)) = DF(v)(ℝⁿ) = range (fderiv ℝ F v) whenever v ∈ C and F(v) ∈ A; and w: E → [0, ∞] an arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) function. Then ∫⁻_{f(A)} w dHⁿ = ∫⁻_A ofReal(jac(Df(y), P(y)))·w(f(y)) dHⁿ(y), where for Λ ∈ L(E, E) and a subspace Q with orthogonal projection p = Q.starProjection, jac(Λ, Q) := (det[⟨Λpe_i, Λpe_j⟩ + ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩]_{i,j ∈ Fin (n+ℓ)})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Ambient n ℓ) (f : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (A : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (P : Ambient n ℓ → Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)) (w : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞), MeasurableSet C → (∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L F) → (∀ v ∈ C, DifferentiableAt ℝ F v) → Set.InjOn F C → (∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L f) → Set.InjOn f A → (∀ y ∈ A, DifferentiableAt ℝ f y) → MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ F '' C → (∀ v ∈ C, F v ∈ A → P (F v) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F v).toLinearMap) → ∫⁻ y in f '' A, w y ∂μHE[n] = ∫⁻ y in A, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (n + ℓ) ↦ inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f y ((P y).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)))) (fderiv ℝ f y ((P y).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))) + inner ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) - (P y).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) - (P y).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))))) * w (f y) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3(b)–(e) of the parent proof ("The area formula on one piece", Simon Ch. 4, 1.5–1.6 with the area formula of Ch. 3 §2 / Ch. 2 §3), together with steps 0 and 3(c) for the tangential Jacobian. The parent applies the argument to its Borel hull A of M_i, with the field y ↦ range DF_i(ψ_i(y)) and the weight u = ofReal(θ ∘ f⁻¹). Here the set A, the field P and the weight w are arbitrary within the stated hypotheses. No errata apply.

Notation. Lⁿ := volume (Lebesgue measure) on ℝⁿ. For a linear map T: U → V between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, normDet(T) ≥ 0 is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg). For a linear subspace Q of U, T|_Q := T ∘ ι_Q: Q → V is the restriction (LinearMap.domRestrict). For Φ: ℝⁿ → E, JΦ(v) := normDet(DΦ(v)), where DΦ(v) = fderiv ℝ Φ v; this is SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt Φ v, and areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet is the unfolding lemma. For y ∈ E put jac(y) := jac(Df(y), P(y)); this is exactly the Real.sqrt (Matrix.det …) expression in the integrand of the statement. L_F and L_f denote Lipschitz constants of F and f.
Imports: the frozen scope does not contain these results. weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, areaJacobianAt and the normDet lemmas become available once Submission.lean adds `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz`, which transitively imports Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet; branches of this run that are already accepted add this import. The statement itself elaborates in the frozen scope.

1. The tangential Jacobian is a norm determinant: jac(Λ, Q) = normDet(Λ|_Q) for every Λ ∈ L(E, E) and every subspace Q ⊆ E. Let k := dim Q and let b be an orthonormal basis of Q indexed by Fin k (e.g. stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q).
- By the sibling theorem ts_fv_det_tangential_gram_eq (with N := n + ℓ, P := Q, this b and Λ), det[⟨Λpe_i, Λpe_j⟩ + ⟨e_i − pe_i, e_j − pe_j⟩]_{i,j} = det[⟨Λb_a, Λb_c⟩]_{a,c}.
- By LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram applied to Λ|_Q and b, normDet(Λ|_Q)² = det Gram((Λ|_Q)(b_a))_a = det[⟨Λb_a, Λb_c⟩]_{a,c}. Here Matrix.gram ℝ v is by definition Matrix.of fun a c ↦ ⟨v a, v c⟩, (Λ|_Q)(b_a) = Λ(b_a), and the coercion ℝ → ℝ in that lemma is the identity.
- Hence the determinant under the square root in jac(Λ, Q) equals normDet(Λ|_Q)². Since normDet(Λ|_Q) ≥ 0, jac(Λ, Q) = √(normDet(Λ|_Q)²) = normDet(Λ|_Q).
In particular jac(y) = normDet(Df(y)|_{P(y)}) ≥ 0 for every y ∈ E.

2. The parameter set. Let B := C ∩ F⁻¹(A).
- B is Borel: F is Lipschitz, hence continuous, so F⁻¹(A) is Borel, and C is Borel.
- F(B) = A. The inclusion F(B) ⊆ A is clear. Conversely, if y ∈ A, then y ∈ F(C) because A ⊆ F(C), so y = F(v) with v ∈ C. Then v ∈ F⁻¹(A), i.e. v ∈ B, and y = F(v) ∈ F(B).
- F is injective on B, because B ⊆ C.

3. The composite map. Let G := f ∘ F.
- G is Lipschitz with constant L_f·L_F (LipschitzWith.comp).
- G is injective on B. Let v, v' ∈ B with f(F(v)) = f(F(v')). Then F(v), F(v') ∈ A and f is injective on A, so F(v) = F(v'). Since F is injective on B, v = v'.
- G(B) = f(F(B)) = f(A) by step 2.

4. Chain rule for the Jacobians. Let v ∈ B. Then v ∈ C, so F is differentiable at v; and F(v) ∈ A, so f is differentiable at F(v). By the chain rule (fderiv_comp), DG(v) = Df(F(v)) ∘ DF(v). LinearMap.normDet_comp says normDet(T₂ ∘ T₁) = normDet(T₂|_{range T₁})·normDet(T₁) for linear maps T₁: U → V and T₂: V → W. Therefore JG(v) = normDet(Df(F(v))|_{range DF(v)})·JF(v). Since v ∈ C and F(v) ∈ A, the hypothesis on P gives range DF(v) = P(F(v)). By step 1, JG(v) = jac(F(v))·JF(v).

5. The weighted area formula. SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn applies to a Lipschitz map Φ: ℝⁿ → E, a Borel set S ⊆ ℝⁿ on which Φ is injective, and an arbitrary g: E → [0, ∞] (no measurability is required). It gives
∫⁻_{Φ(S)} g dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝⁿ] = ∫⁻_S ofReal(JΦ(v))·g(Φ(v)) dLⁿ(v).
Here finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so the measure on the left is Hⁿ.
(a) Take Φ = G, S = B, g = w; the hypotheses hold by steps 2 and 3. Since G(B) = f(A):
∫⁻_{f(A)} w dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JG(v))·w(f(F(v))) dLⁿ(v).
(b) Take Φ = F, S = B, g = h, where h(y) := ofReal(jac(y))·w(f(y)); the hypotheses hold by step 2. Since F(B) = A:
∫⁻_A ofReal(jac(y))·w(f(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(JF(v))·ofReal(jac(F(v)))·w(f(F(v))) dLⁿ(v).

6. Comparison of the integrands. Let v ∈ B. By step 4 and ENNReal.ofReal_mul (applicable since jac(F(v)) ≥ 0 by step 1),
ofReal(JG(v))·w(f(F(v))) = ofReal(jac(F(v)))·ofReal(JF(v))·w(f(F(v))) = ofReal(JF(v))·ofReal(jac(F(v)))·w(f(F(v))).
So the integrands of 5(a) and 5(b) agree at every point of the Borel set B, and the two integrals over B are equal (setLIntegral_congr_fun). Combining 5(a), this equality and 5(b):
∫⁻_{f(A)} w dHⁿ = ∫⁻_A ofReal(jac(y))·w(f(y)) dHⁿ(y).
This is the claim, since jac(y) is the Real.sqrt (Matrix.det …) expression of the statement with Λ = Df(y) = fderiv ℝ f y and Q = P(y).

7. Degenerate cases. No step uses n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1 or A ≠ ∅, and weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn has no dimension or nonemptiness hypothesis. So the argument applies verbatim when n = 0 and when A = ∅ (then both sides vanish). If n = 0, ℝⁿ is a single point and step 1 still applies, including to Q = 0, where both sides equal 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: jac(Λ, Q) = normDet(Λ|_Q): sibling ts_fv_det_tangential_gram_eq with an orthonormal basis b of Q, LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram and normDet ≥ 0
B := C ∩ F⁻¹(A) is Borel with F(B) = A and F injective on B; G := f ∘ F is Lipschitz, injective on B, and G(B) = f(A)
For v ∈ B: fderiv_comp, LinearMap.normDet_comp and P(F v) = range DF(v) give JG(v) = jac(F v)·JF(v)
weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn for G with weight w and for F with weight ofReal(jac)·(w ∘ f); the integrands over B agree pointwise
